sections.title: All moderation database calls
sections.what: Groups every database call for moderation in one place: create a report, list open reports, mark a report resolved only for the matching crew, look up names, add or remove a block, list blocked ids, list owned crews and check a user exists. The reporting, blocking and owner features all rely on it.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps moderation storage separate from the rules that use it.
sections.watch_out: The resolve and block rules depend on these query filters, so changing a filter can let an owner act on another crew.

summary: Database queries for crew reports, user blocks and crew ownership checks.
purpose: Keeps the database work for reporting and blocking in one place for the moderation service.
why: Likely reason: the same separation of storage from rules used elsewhere in the app.
how: 1. Creates a report. 2. Lists open reports for a crew. 3. Marks a report resolved only if it belongs to that crew. 4. Looks up names for a list of user ids. 5. Creates or removes a block, and lists who a user has blocked. 6. Lists the crews a user owns and checks that a user exists.
inputs: Crew id, reporter and reported user ids, reason, note and other ids.
outputs: Created report ids, report rows, counts, names, block rows, crew ids and yes or no answers.
risks: Blocks are one way: blocking someone does not block the reverse. Removing a block only removes that one pair.
debug: If reports do not appear, check that the status is OPEN and the crew id is right. If a block seems to fail, check that the user exists and that the pair is the right way round.
